questions.markdown: A thin cylindrical shell is 3.5m long and 1.2m in internal diameter. It is subjected to internal pressure of 1.4 MPa. If the thickness of the sheet is 10mm, find the circumferential stress and longitudinal stress. Take $E=200\ \text{GPa}$ and $\mu = 0.3$.

A rectangular bar of $300\ \text{mm}$ length is $100\ \text{mm}$ wide and $30\ \text{mm}$ thick. It is loaded with an axial tensile load of $200\ \text{kN}$, together with a normal compressive force of $500\ \text{kN}$ on the face $100\ \text{mm} \times 300\ \text{mm}$ and a tensile force $400\ \text{kN}$ on the face $30\ \text{mm} \times 300\ \text{mm}$. Calculate the Poisson's ratio, strain in all the three directions if the change in volume is $195.408\ \text{mm}^3$ and also find the change in dimension in the direction of $500\ \text{kN}$ load. questions.markdown: A steel hollow tube of internal diameter $50\ \text{mm}$ and thickness $10\ \text{mm}$ has a solid rod of copper of diameter $50\ \text{mm}$ placed snuggly inside it. The compound bar thus formed is rigidly joined at their contact surfaces at a temperature of $20^\circ\text{C}$. Determine the stresses in steel and copper if the temperature is raised to $40^\circ\text{C}$. Take $E_{steel} = 200\ \text{GPa}$ and $E_{copper} = 100\ \text{GPa}$. Also, temperature expansion coefficient of steel and copper are $1 \times 10^{-6}/^\circ\text{C}$ and $1.5 \times 10^{-6}/^\circ\text{C}$ respectively.

A hollow steel pipe of internal diameter $100\ \text{mm}$ is filled with concrete inside. What must be the thickness of the steel pipe required such that under the action of axial force $P$, both steel and concrete will carry equal load ? $E_{steel} = 200\ \text{GPa}$ and $E_{concrete} = 30\ \text{GPa}$.
